## Notation for Chapters 1--12 {#sec-p2-concepts-notation .unnumbered}

| Group | Symbol (preferred form) | Meaning | Main use | Alternatives and notes |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Indices and counts | $i$, $j$, $k$; $n$, $p$, $m$ | Unit, indicator and factor indices; numbers of units, indicators and factors | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.1 | $p=6$ and $m=2$ throughout Chapter 1's running system; $N$ writes the analysis sample size in the likelihood conventions of Chapter 3, Sec. 7 and Chapter 4, Sec. 2; $a$ also serves as a factor index in Chapters 2--3 |
| Observed | $y_{ij}$, $\mathbf y_i$, $Y_j$ | One response, the $p\times1$ response vector for unit $i$, and the indicator as a random variable | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.1--2.2 | Uppercase only where the distinction from an observed value matters |
| Model | $\boldsymbol\nu$, $\nu_j$ | The $p\times1$ vector of indicator intercepts | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.1--2.2 | --- |
| Model | $\boldsymbol\Lambda$, $\boldsymbol\lambda_j$, $\lambda_{jk}$ | The $p\times m$ loading (pattern) matrix, its $j$th row as a column vector, and the entry relating indicator $j$ to factor $k$ | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.2, 3 | Rows are indicators and columns are factors; $\boldsymbol\Lambda_{\text{simple}}$ for the restricted pattern; $\boldsymbol\Lambda_l$ is the first-order loading matrix of Chapter 4, Sec. 5; Part One's notation uses $\lambda$ for the Poisson rate (Part One Chapters 2 and 12) and the penalty size (Part One Chapter 13), so the loading reading is stated at first use |
| Model | $\boldsymbol\eta_i$, $\eta_{ik}$ | The $m\times1$ vector of common factors for unit $i$ and one factor value | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.1 | $\boldsymbol\eta_i^{*}$ for a rescaled, sign-reversed, shifted or rotated version; $\eta$ is the GLM linear predictor in Part One's notation (Part One Chapter 11) and $\eta^{2}$ an ANOVA effect size (Part One Chapter 4), so the factor reading is stated at first use |
| Model | $\boldsymbol\epsilon_i$, $\epsilon_{ij}$ | The $p\times1$ residual vector and one residual | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.1 | Never called measurement error without an argument |
| Model | $\boldsymbol\alpha$ | The $m\times1$ latent intercept vector; the factor mean only where no structural paths exist | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.2 | With $\mathbf B$ present, $E(\boldsymbol\eta_i)=(\mathbf I-\mathbf B)^{-1}\boldsymbol\alpha$; no $\boldsymbol\kappa$ convention; Part One's notation uses $\alpha$ for the Type I error probability (Part One Chapter 3) and the elastic-net mixing parameter (Part One Chapter 13) |
| Model | $\boldsymbol\Phi$, $\phi_{jk}$ | The $m\times m$ factor covariance matrix and its entries; $\boldsymbol\Phi_{2\rho}$ for the correlated two-factor case | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.2, 6.4 | Total latent covariance across the series, not a disturbance covariance $\boldsymbol\Psi$; $\boldsymbol\Phi_l$ is the first-order factor covariance matrix of Chapter 4, Sec. 5; Part One's notation uses $\Phi$ for the standard Normal distribution function (Part One Chapter 2) |
| Model | $\boldsymbol\Theta$, $\theta_{jk}$ | The $p\times p$ residual covariance matrix and its entries | Chapter 1, Sec. 2.2--2.3 | $\operatorname{diag}(\theta_{11},\ldots,\theta_{pp})$ for the diagonal working version; the parameter space is $\mathcal P$, never another $\Theta$; Part One's notation uses $\theta$, $\widehat\theta$ for a generic estimand (Part One Chapter 3) and the negative-binomial dispersion (Part One Chapter 12) |
| Implied moments | $\boldsymbol\vartheta$, $\boldsymbol\Sigma(\boldsymbol\vartheta)$, $\boldsymbol\mu(\boldsymbol\vartheta)$ | The free-parameter vector and the implied covariance and mean it produces | Chapter 1, Sec. 5 | $\boldsymbol\Sigma$ alone where the argument is clear; Chapter 3, Sec. 1 reads $\boldsymbol\vartheta$ as the complete free-parameter vector, distinct from $\boldsymbol\Theta$ |
| Implied moments | $h_j^{2}$ | The communality of indicator $j$ under the declared model | Chapter 1, Sec. 5.1 | $\theta_{jj}=1-h_j^{2}$ for a standardized indicator; written as the quadratic form $\mathbf p_j^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\Phi\mathbf p_j$ in Chapter 2, Sec. 6.2 and for a cross-loading indicator in Chapter 3, Sec. 8; $u_j^{2}$ writes the matching uniqueness in Chapter 2 |
| Counting | $u$, $t$, $df$ | Distinct observed moments, free parameters, and their difference | Chapter 1, Sec. 5.3 | $df$ upright; $u=21$ for six indicators; reused in Chapter 3, Sec. 6; the subscripted $u_j^{2}$ of Chapter 2 is a uniqueness, not a moment count; an unsubscripted $t$ here is the free-parameter count, distinct from the Part One $t_{df}$ reference distribution (Part One Chapter 3) |
| Counting | $u_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $u_{\mathrm{mean+cov}}$ | Moment counts without and with an unrestricted mean vector | Chapter 3, Sec. 5 | Free indicator intercepts with latent intercepts fixed add equally to moments and parameters, leaving $df$ unchanged |
| Counting | $t_m$ | The effective parameter count of an unrestricted $m$-factor solution, $pm+p-m(m-1)/2$ | Chapter 2, Sec. 4.1 | The unrestricted-EFA dimension of Chapter 3, Sec. 6 is the same count; an unsubscripted $t$ is the free-parameter count of Chapter 1, Sec. 5.3 |
| Coordinates | $a$, $\mathbf c$, $\mathbf Q$ | A nonzero rescaling constant, an $m\times1$ location shift, and an orthogonal coordinate matrix | Chapter 1, Sec. 4.1--4.2, 7 | $\mathbf T$ for the general invertible transformation is Chapter 2's; $\mathbf Q$ is the orthogonal rotation matrix of Chapter 2, Sec. 5.2; $a$ also indexes factors in $p_{ja}$, $\lambda_{ja}$ and $\phi_{aa}$ (Chapters 2--3) and names $\boldsymbol\lambda^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\Theta^{-1}\boldsymbol\lambda$ in coefficient $H$ (Chapter 4, Appendix), so the setting is stated at first use |
| Coordinates | $\mathbf T$ | The general nonsingular change of factor coordinates, $\boldsymbol\Lambda\mathbf T^{-1}$ paired with $\mathbf T\boldsymbol\Phi\mathbf T^{\mathsf T}$ | Chapter 2, Sec. 5.1 | Reused for the rotational family in Chapter 3, Sec. 6; the orthogonal case keeps Chapter 1's $\mathbf Q$ |
| Coordinates | $\gamma$, $\delta$ | The oblimin parameter and the geomin parameter of the rotation criteria | Chapter 2, Sec. 5.2 | Plain letters; the bold $\boldsymbol\gamma$ and $\boldsymbol\delta$ of Chapter 4, Sec. 5 are second-order loadings and first-order disturbances |
| Classical test theory | $X_{ir}$, $T_i$, $E_{ir}$ | Observed score on repetition $r$, true score, and error | Chapter 1, Sec. 1.2 | $E_r(\cdot\mid i)$ averages over repetitions with the person fixed |
| Scores | $\widehat{\eta}_{ik}$ | A factor-score estimate for unit $i$ on factor $k$ | Chapter 1, Sec. 6.5 | The hat marks a prediction from a fitted model, never the factor; $\mathbf A_R$ and $\mathbf A_B$ of Chapter 4, Appendix supply the weights |
| Fixed arrays | $\mathbf I_p$, $\mathbf 1_p$, $\operatorname{diag}(\cdot)$ | The $p\times p$ identity, the $p\times1$ vector of ones, and the diagonal matrix formed from the listed entries | Chapter 1, Sec. 6.1--6.2 | $\mathbf 1_6$ writes the one-factor record's equal loadings as $.7\,\mathbf 1_6$ |
| Sample records | $\mathbf S$, $\mathbf R$ | The sample covariance matrix, divisor $n-1$, and the sample Pearson correlation matrix | Chapter 2 | Reserved in Chapter 1, which has no sample and uses $\mathbf S$ only for its rescaling anchor; the structure matrix is written $\boldsymbol\Lambda\boldsymbol\Phi$ and given no symbol; Part One's notation homes both as observed-variable matrices and, like Part Two, writes matrices and vectors bold with a superscript $\mathsf T$ for the transpose |
| Sample records | $\mathbf D_S$ | The diagonal matrix of sample variances | Chapter 2 | $\mathbf D_y$ is the observed-variance counterpart in the correlation reparameterization of Chapter 3, Sec. 4 |
| Sample records | $\mathbf V$, $\mathbf D$, $d_k$ | Eigenvectors, the eigenvalue matrix, and the $k$th eigenvalue of $\mathbf R$ | Chapter 2 | A spectral eigenvalue matrix; the $\mathbf D$ of Chapter 3, Sec. 4 is the diagonal factor-scale transformation and Part One's notation uses $\mathbf D$ for a diagonal SD matrix, $\widehat{\mathbf V}$ for estimated coefficient covariance (Part One Chapter 8) and $d$ for Cohen's $d$ (Part One Chapter 3), so the setting is named at first use |
| Sample records | $\mathbf R_c^{(t)}$ | The reduced correlation matrix at iteration $t$ | Chapter 2, Sec. 2.3 | The superscript is an iteration index, not the free-parameter count $t$; the reduced matrix need not be positive semidefinite |
| Extraction | $\mathbf A$, $\mathbf A_m$ | The unrotated loading matrix and its rank-$m$ PCA counterpart | Chapter 2 | $\mathbf A$ is the parcel weight matrix in Chapter 3, Appendix and $\mathbf A_R$, $\mathbf A_B$ are factor-score weight matrices in Chapter 4, Appendix; each use is declared locally |
| Extraction | $F_{\mathrm{minres}}$ | The minimum-residual extraction discrepancy | Chapter 2, Sec. 2.4 | A common-factor criterion, not another name for principal-axis factoring |
| Retention | $SS_k$ | The sum of squared loadings in column $k$ | Chapter 2, Sec. 3.2 | Generally not a spectral eigenvalue, and distinct from the Part One ANOVA $SS$ family |
| Retention | $B$, $Q_{.95}$ | The number of permutation replications and the 95th-percentile null reference | Chapter 2, Sec. 3.4 | The bold $\mathbf B$ of Chapter 4, Sec. 8 is the latent structural path matrix |
| Retention | $\text{EKC}_j$ | The empirical Kaiser reference for root $j$ | Chapter 2, Sec. 3.5 | Built on the Marchenko--Pastur bound $(1+\sqrt{p/n})^2$ and floored at one |
| Retention | $T_m$, $df_m$ | The corrected exploratory model statistic for $m$ factors and its degrees of freedom | Chapter 2, Sec. 3.5 | Lowercase $m$ marks the exploratory sequence; the uppercase $T_M$, $df_M$ of Chapter 4, Sec. 2 are the confirmatory model statistic and its degrees of freedom |
| Rotation | $\mathbf P$, $p_{ja}$ | The pattern matrix and the pattern coefficient of indicator $j$ on factor $a$ | Chapter 2, Sec. 6.1 | $\boldsymbol\Lambda$ names the same object in the model equations of Chapter 1 and Chapter 3 |
| Rotation | $\mathbf C$ | The structure matrix $\mathbf C=\mathbf P\boldsymbol\Phi$ of indicator--factor correlations | Chapter 2, Sec. 6.1 | Defined as $\boldsymbol\Lambda\boldsymbol\Phi$ in Chapter 1, Sec. 5, which gives it no symbol |
| Residual evidence | $\mathbf E$, $e_{jk}$, $\mathrm{RMS}_{\mathrm{off}}$ | The correlation residual matrix, its entries, and the off-diagonal summary $\sqrt{2\sum_{j<k}e_{jk}^2/[p(p-1)]}$ | Chapter 2, Sec. 7.1 | In Chapter 4, Sec. 3 $e_{jk}$ is the raw covariance residual and $e^{(s)}_{jk}$, $e^{(r)}_{jk}$ the standardized and correlation scales, so the scale is always named; this summary is not automatically any software RMSR or SRMR |
| Residual evidence | $\widehat r_{jk}$ | A reproduced correlation | Chapter 2, Sec. 7.1 | The hat marks a model-implied value, not a sample statistic |
| Preliminary summaries | $a_{jk}$ | A partial correlation entering the KMO ratio | Chapter 2, Sec. 7.2 | Distinct from the rescaling constant $a$ of Chapter 1, Sec. 4.1 and from the factor index $a$ |
| Preliminary summaries | $T_B$, $df_B$ | Bartlett's sphericity statistic and its $p(p-1)/2$ degrees of freedom | Chapter 2, Sec. 7.2 | In Chapter 4, Sec. 2 the same pair names the independence-baseline statistic of the incremental indices, a different null |
| Analytic sensitivity | $c(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ | Tucker's congruence coefficient between two loading columns $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ | Chapter 2, Sec. 7.3 | Compared after column order and sign are aligned; these are loading columns, not the shift vector $\mathbf b$ of Chapter 3, Sec. 4 |
| Parameter space | $\mathcal P$ | The admissible parameter space | Chapter 3, Sec. 7 | Never written $\Theta$, which is the residual covariance matrix |
| Latent metric | $\mathbf D$ (factor scale) | The diagonal factor-scale transformation, $\boldsymbol\Lambda^*=\boldsymbol\Lambda\mathbf D^{-1}$ with $\boldsymbol\Phi^*=\mathbf D\boldsymbol\Phi\mathbf D^{\mathsf T}$ | Chapter 3, Sec. 4 | Carries its qualifier, because $\mathbf D$ is also the eigenvalue matrix of Chapter 2 |
| Latent metric | $\lambda_{ja}^{(\mathrm{lv})}$, $\lambda_{ja}^{(\mathrm{all})}$ | Latent-standardized and fully standardized loadings | Chapter 3, Sec. 4 | $\lambda\sqrt{\phi_{aa}}$ and $\lambda\sqrt{\phi_{aa}}/\sqrt{\sigma_{jj}}$; a raw standard error is not the standardized coefficient's standard error |
| Observed units | $\boldsymbol\Delta$, $\mathbf b$ | The diagonal observed-unit conversion matrix and its shift vector, giving $\mathbf b+\boldsymbol\Delta\mathbf y$ | Chapter 3, Sec. 4 | Reserved for observed-unit rescaling across Part Two and named without algebra in Chapter 1; the moment Jacobian is written $\partial\mathbf s/\partial\boldsymbol\vartheta^{\mathsf T}$, never $\boldsymbol\Delta$. Chapter 3, Sec. 6.5 writes the moment Jacobian in that form, and the Chapter 4 local-rank check inherits it; Part Two keeps the two symbols separate |
| Observed units | $\mathbf D_y$ | The diagonal matrix of observed variances used in the correlation reparameterization | Chapter 3, Sec. 4 | $\mathbf R=\mathbf D_y^{-1/2}\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf D_y^{-1/2}$; $\mathbf D_S$ of Chapter 2 is the sample counterpart |
| Observed units | $\mathbf R$ (implied correlation) | The model-implied correlation matrix | Chapter 3, Sec. 4 | Carries its qualifier: an unqualified $\mathbf R$ is the sample correlation matrix of Chapter 2 |
| Identification | $\mathbf s(\boldsymbol\vartheta)$, $\partial\mathbf s/\partial\boldsymbol\vartheta^{\mathsf T}$ | The stacked implied moments and their Jacobian | Chapter 3, Sec. 6 | Full column rank at a regular fitted point supports local identification only |
| Estimation | $F_{\mathrm{ML}}$ | The normal-theory ML discrepancy | Chapter 3, Sec. 7 (first used Chapter 2, Sec. 2.4) | $\widehat F_{\mathrm{ML}}$ at the fitted point enters $T_M=N\widehat F_{\mathrm{ML}}$ in Chapter 4, Sec. 2; rotation does not change it |
| Estimation | $\mathbf S_N$, $\mathbf S_{N-1}$ | The sample covariance matrix under the two divisor conventions, $\mathbf S_N=\{(N-1)/N\}\mathbf S_{N-1}$ | Chapter 3, Sec. 7 | $\mathbf S_N$ is reused in Chapter 4, Sec. 2; the convention is disclosed and never applied twice |
| Inference | $\mathbf R$ (restriction), $\mathbf r$, $q$, $W$ | The restriction rows, their values, their number, and the Wald statistic for $\mathbf R\boldsymbol\vartheta=\mathbf r$ | Chapter 3, Sec. 8 | Carries its qualifier; this $q$ counts restrictions, while the $q$ of Chapter 4, Sec. 4 is an effective free-parameter count |
| Parcels | $\mathbf A$ (parcel), $\mathbf z$ | The parcel weight matrix and the parcel score vector, with $\operatorname{Var}(\mathbf z)=\mathbf A\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf A^{\mathsf T}$ | Chapter 3, Appendix | Carries its qualifier beside the extraction and factor-score uses of $\mathbf A$ |
| Global fit | $T_M$, $df_M$ | The model test statistic $N\widehat F_{\mathrm{ML}}$ and the model degrees of freedom of the declared covariance model | Chapter 4, Sec. 2 | Uppercase $M$; the lowercase $T_m$, $df_m$ of Chapter 2, Sec. 3.5 belong to the exploratory sequence |
| Global fit | $T_B$ (baseline), $df_B$ | The independence-baseline statistic and its degrees of freedom in CFI and TLI | Chapter 4, Sec. 2 | Carries its qualifier; the same pair is Bartlett's sphericity test in Chapter 2, Sec. 7.2 |
| Local diagnosis | $e_{jk}$, $e^{(s)}_{jk}$, $e^{(r)}_{jk}$ | Raw, observed-SD-standardized, and correlation covariance residuals | Chapter 4, Sec. 3 | None is divided by a sampling standard error, so none is a $z$ statistic; $e_{jk}$ is the correlation residual in Chapter 2, Sec. 7.1, so the scale is named |
| Comparison | $\Delta T$, $\Delta df$ | The nested difference statistic and its degrees of freedom | Chapter 4, Sec. 4 | For regularly nested, compatible ML fits on identical cases, outcomes, scale, mean structure, and likelihood convention |
| Comparison | $\ell(\widehat{\boldsymbol\vartheta})$, $q$ | The maximized log likelihood and the effective free-parameter count in $-2\ell+2q$ and $-2\ell+q\log N$ | Chapter 4, Sec. 4 | This $q$ is a parameter count; the $q$ of Chapter 3, Sec. 8 counts restriction rows |
| Extensions | $\boldsymbol\gamma$ | The $m\times1$ second-order loading vector | Chapter 4, Sec. 5 | Bold; the plain $\gamma$ of Chapter 2, Sec. 5.2 is the oblimin parameter |
| Extensions | $\boldsymbol\delta$, $\boldsymbol\Psi_h$, $\psi_{h,k}$ | First-order disturbances, their diagonal covariance matrix, and its $k$th diagonal entry, with $\boldsymbol\Phi_l=\boldsymbol\gamma\boldsymbol\gamma^{\mathsf T}+\boldsymbol\Psi_h$ | Chapter 4, Sec. 5 | Bold; the plain $\delta$ of Chapter 2, Sec. 5.2 is the geomin parameter. First-order disturbances are not indicator residuals |
| Extensions | $\boldsymbol\Lambda_l$, $\boldsymbol\Phi_l$ | The first-order loading matrix and first-order factor covariance matrix of the higher-order form | Chapter 4, Sec. 5 | The subscript $l$ marks the first-order level |
| Extensions | $\lambda_{jg}$, $\lambda_{js}$; $G$, $S_{is}$ | Bifactor general and specific loadings for item $j$; the general factor and the specific factor for unit $i$ in domain $s$ | Chapter 4, Sec. 5 | $S_{is}$ is a specific factor, not an entry of the sample covariance matrix $\mathbf S$ |
| Reliability and scores | $\mathbf w$, $c_i$ | Declared score weights and the composite for unit $i$ | Chapter 4, Sec. 8 | The weights are declared before any coefficient is calculated |
| Reliability and scores | $\omega(\mathbf w)$, $\omega_h(\mathbf w)$ | The model-based common-variance proportion for those weights and omega-hierarchical | Chapter 4, Secs. 8 and 5 | Both are conditional on model, weights, and sample |
| Reliability and scores | $H$ | Coefficient $H$ under a restrictive one-factor model, $H=a/(1+a)$ with $a=\boldsymbol\lambda^{\mathsf T}\boldsymbol\Theta^{-1}\boldsymbol\lambda$ | Chapter 4, Appendix | Plain; Part One's notation uses the bold $\mathbf H$ for the regression hat matrix |
| Reliability and scores | $\mathbf A_R$, $\mathbf A_B$ | Regression and Bartlett factor-score weight matrices | Chapter 4, Appendix | $\widehat{\eta}_{ik}$ of Chapter 1, Sec. 6.5 is the resulting prediction |
| Population audit | $\boldsymbol\Sigma_0$, $\boldsymbol\Sigma^{*}$ | The exact generating covariance and its pseudo-true fitted counterpart | Chapter 4, Sec. 7 | Displacement at the pseudo-true optimum is deterministic, not sampling fluctuation |
| Population audit | $F_0$, $\operatorname{RMSEA}_0$ | The population discrepancy and the population RMSEA $\sqrt{F_0/df}$ | Chapter 4, Sec. 7 | Not the sample RMSEA formula |
| Structural extension | $\mathbf B$, $\boldsymbol\Gamma$, $\boldsymbol\zeta$, $\boldsymbol\Psi$ | Latent structural paths, exogenous links, the structural disturbance, and its covariance | Chapter 4, Sec. 8 | Bold $\mathbf B$; the plain $B$ of Chapter 2, Sec. 3.4 is a replication count. The bare $\boldsymbol\Psi$ is the structural disturbance covariance and nothing else: the Schmid-Leiman equations of Chapter 4, Sec. 5.5 write the first-order disturbance covariance as $\boldsymbol\Psi_h$ |
